beats.text: This is jaiscloud, a local emulator for Google Cloud. We point real Google clients and real Terraform at it, and run one crypto data product through its whole life: provision, ingest, process, serve, observe and automate.
beats.ssml: This is jaiscloud, a local emulator for Google Cloud. We point real Google clients and real Terraform at it, and run one crypto data product through its whole life: provision, ingest, process, serve, observe and automate.

beats.text: Provision starts with Terraform. It creates the project's Cloud Storage buckets, then a Cloud KMS key ring and key for encryption, then the Secret Manager entry the bridge reads, a Pub/Sub topic for events, and the demo service account.
beats.ssml: Provision starts with Terraform. It creates the project's <mark name="buckets"/>Cloud Storage buckets, then a <mark name="kms"/>Cloud KMS key ring and key for encryption, then the <mark name="secret"/>Secret Manager entry the bridge reads, a <mark name="pubsub"/>Pub/Sub topic for events, and the demo <mark name="iam"/>service account.

beats.text: Then gcloud creates the data platform: the Managed Kafka cluster and its trades topic, and the Dataproc cluster the Spark jobs run on.
beats.ssml: Then gcloud creates the data platform: the <mark name="kafka"/>Managed Kafka cluster and its <mark name="topic"/>trades topic, and the <mark name="dataproc"/>Dataproc cluster the Spark jobs run on.

beats.text: Ingest. A bridge pod reads a live public trade feed, normalizes every trade, and produces it to Managed Kafka. Every run also writes the raw stream to this capture bucket.
beats.ssml: Ingest. A bridge pod reads a live public trade feed, normalizes every trade, and produces it to <mark name="topic"/>Managed Kafka. Every run also writes the raw stream to this <mark name="capture"/>capture bucket.

beats.text: Process. One always-on Dataproc job reads the topic and writes the medallion: raw bronze, parsed silver, and a windowed gold table in Iceberg on the Hive Metastore.
beats.ssml: Process. One always-on <mark name="job"/>Dataproc job reads the topic and writes the medallion: raw bronze, parsed silver, and a windowed <mark name="gold"/>gold table in Iceberg on the Hive Metastore.

beats.text: Serve. Every gold rollup fires Eventarc, which drives a Cloud Run publisher into Firestore for the live read model, and into BigQuery for the warehouse. This leaderboard re-sorts as each window lands.
beats.ssml: Serve. Every gold rollup fires <mark name="eventarc"/>Eventarc, which drives a <mark name="run"/>Cloud Run publisher into <mark name="firestore"/>Firestore for the live read model, and into <mark name="bigquery"/>BigQuery for the warehouse. This leaderboard re-sorts as each window lands.

beats.text: Observe. A custom metric, trades per minute, crosses an alert policy and opens an incident, delivered as a message on the Pub/Sub subscription.
beats.ssml: Observe. A custom <mark name="metric"/>metric, trades per minute, crosses an <mark name="alert"/>alert policy and opens an incident, delivered as a <mark name="message"/>message on the Pub/Sub subscription.

beats.text: Automate. Cloud Scheduler submits the batch rollup on a cron, the load job lands it in BigQuery, and every component writes structured entries to Cloud Logging. And it all runs locally.
beats.ssml: Automate. <mark name="scheduler"/>Cloud Scheduler submits the batch rollup on a cron, the <mark name="bqjobs"/>load job lands it in BigQuery, and every component writes structured entries to <mark name="logging"/>Cloud Logging. And it all runs locally.
